Additionally, the rewards feel repetitive and don’t change much, which takes away some motivation to keep progressing. I still enjoy the game a lot and hope these issues can be improved in future updates.

A neat concept but….. The game is a cool concept, but that’s all I can say nice about it.  The charm quickly wears off as you are quickly assaulted by ads.

- Want to get all the power ups for a round?  Watch an ad.
- Oh boy the difficulty is ramping up quickly.  Better watch that ad to get those power ups now.
- Ooops you died to a tough wave?  Better watch that ad to revive, and oh no the ad broke the wave and you can’t complete the stage. 
- Oh wow you really are going to need the free currency to power up faster, better watch an ad to double your rewards. 
- Oh hey you also get a “spell pack” to unlock a single hidden card out of 3 which represent new power ups for a stage. Want to get another random card of 3?  That’s gonna be another ad. 

And you pretty much get the idea. Not to mention since the whole premise of the game is built on RNG that you can only adjust by buying power ups or hoping for the right power up to appear.  And as soon as you hit the second area you are hit by a bunch of micro transactions to further power up your characters. Just not worth it and uninstalled.

This game forces you into 5-6 ads in a 15 minute session. It’s absolutely egregious, and what’s sad is that it’s a great game, it’s an interesting idea, the app is well polished, just be prepared to pay 6.99 if you want to play for real. And the bonuses in the shop for spending money are too great. This game makes you feel like if you aren’t spending money or watching 5 ads every 20 minutes that you’re seriously missing out. Watching ads should be a bonus, spending money should give you a slight to moderate advantage.

What the design of this game tells me is that whoever was in charge of monetization never actually played the game, is greedy, and/or doesn’t think the game will survive on its own merits.

This game feels like it was bought by a private equity firm, it’s being exploited like Red Lobster. 

You can make money off your game, but make the people who run monetization actually play it, ask them, is this fun if you don’t buy? If it isn’t, your monetization is bad. You need F2P players, they will *always* be your lifeblood and you’re going to lose them with this setup. You might be losing me and this sort of game is my jam.

Lots of Potential, Not There Yet. The game itself is fun and has a lot of potential, but it pushes you very hard to spend money. I gave in and bought a couple of things, starting with the ad free option and later Electra. The ad free option makes the game feel much easier since you can collect all three cards at once without watching ads. It lets you breeze through the early levels until about level 20, when the game becomes more challenging. I am currently at level 33 and depending on which character I use it can take some time to get through the mobs.

I also spent over forty dollars on Electra to see if she would make a real difference compared to the free characters. She is level 53 now, but I actually prefer the Knight at the same level. Her abilities look flashier, but she is not stronger than the free characters you already get. In fact, I still prefer the Mage since his abilities deal more damage more quickly than most.

Survival mode is a nice addition since it helps you earn more coins for castle and armor upgrades, but the game does become repetitive. The monsters cycle on rotation with little variety, and I have run into bugs. For example, when I reached level 100, the castle health upgrade did not actually unlock for me.

Overall, Dice vs Monsters has potential, but at the moment it feels more like a money grab than a balanced game. If you want to play, I recommend sticking to the free content. Extra characters are not worth the money.

1. If you play this game and decide to make purchases, and idk if it is just me, but keep in mind that there is apparently no account linking to save historical game data. A while ago I made a few purchases for a character I liked, ad removals, and the gameplay perma speedup bonus, but it's now all gone. I took a break, uninstalled the game, reinstalled it to see what updates were made, and all my purchases were gone. With no option to log in or connect to an account, I chose the option to restore purchases, but nothing happened.

2. Speaking of purchases, i love supporting free games and I get companies have to make money, but the cost for almost everything is ludicrous. Pure insanity. Truly. $60 for ad removal on a mobile game? How in the world is this game worth that when it's just a mobile game, you do not get all the content, and still have to pay an insane amount to unlock content such as the other heroes? The heroes, btw, are mostly between the $35-$60 range and they don't come with everything unlocked. You can still make additional purchases for their level boosting and ability unlocks, which are also crazy expensive.

3. The progression system is WEAK. Gear takes forever to farm with minimal opportunities to get gear. The gear upgrading is slow. The abilities are easy to unlock with minimal to no advancement after they are upgraded. The upgrading of abilities is also far too easy and ends quickly with a bug that allows you to upgrade at the cost of 32 resources vs the intended 56. There aren't many characters to unlock yourself, you get them fast (except for one that requires continuous play for a month). The castle mechanic is flat with upgrades unlocked early and only one set of options (not actually customizable).

4. Balancing is a serious issue here as well. There are clearly superior ability choices to choose from and one route that will take you significantly farther in the game. It's not even complex. Even heroes themselves and their upgrades/abilities are significantly imbalanced compared to one another. There is literally one free hero that can take you twice as far in the game with fewer upgrades.

5. There is a major lack of content. Again, the gameplay is fun, but there is really only one thing you will do in the entire game. No PvP. No unique rounds. Systematic repetition in quantities for various stages, etc.

Fun for a month. The game was really interesting and fun for a while when I first downloaded it. There was a feeling of progression and it was fun to unlock new characters. But especially after a recent update, the progression has come to a grinding halt. When a new character unlocks, they are now severely underleveled compared to the rest of your characters, meaning you won’t want to use them until they’ve leveled up more. But even when I do use my stronger characters, it feels like 80% of the time I lose a battle without ever killing a single minion. The attacks target the closest minion, and when they start to form up at the bottom, you spread your attacks out against them all instead of targeting the weakest one, so you never earn an upgrade and just sit waiting to lose. Also there is no way to forfeit a battle when you already know you’re going to lose, so you just have to wait for it to play itself out. There are 3 additional characters that require real life currency purchase to access, but it just doesn’t feel like a worthwhile investment. It’s a shame, I really enjoyed this game for a while, but now it’s usually more of a chore to play.

These ads are ALL double-skip ads (Where you can’t exit the ad until clicking the third time), which is very annoying. Lastly, this form of ad scaling is highly manipulative, as you don’t always want to stop playing if you’ve already sunk time into the game without egregious ads at the start, so when they start popping up all the time your brain might think “Well, I already sunk an hour into this, might as well keep playing”.
